subject.title: /learn's skill-authoring-and-apply pipeline has no owner gate, unlike the equivalent plugin-install path

question: Where should OpenClaw enforce owner-tier authorization for Skill Workshop authoring and lifecycle approval: `/learn`, `skill_workshop` lifecycle execution, `/approve` plugin approval resolution, or all of those layers?
rationale: The source-level bypass is concrete, but choosing only one enforcement layer could leave another entry point open, while enforcing every layer changes a security boundary across chat commands, agent tools, and approval routing.

options.title: Enforce owner at every mutation boundary
options.body: Require owner-tier authority before `/learn` starts Skill Workshop authoring, before lifecycle apply/reject/quarantine executes, and before `/approve` resolves those plugin approval decisions.

options.title: Gate only chat entry points
options.body: Block non-owner `/learn` and `/approve` use while leaving lower-level service/tool calls governed by existing approval policy, which is smaller but trusts callers more heavily.

options.title: Fold into the broader approval-evidence design
options.body: Handle this with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/93278, accepting that the concrete bypass remains open until the broader model is decided.

recommendation.title: Enforce owner at every mutation boundary
recommendation.body: Require owner-tier authority before `/learn` starts Skill Workshop authoring, before lifecycle apply/reject/quarantine executes, and before `/approve` resolves those plugin approval decisions.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is centered on same-chat approval routing and owner authorization semantics, where this history is strongest.
